common.why: The request asks the API to treat it as a different method (_method). Counterseal matches its rules on the real method, so these always wait for a human.

irreversible.why: Any DELETE on GitHub removes something (repo, branch, release, key, member).
Force-updating a ref rewrites history and can drop commits for everyone.
Transferring a repository hands it to another owner.
Changing visibility can publish private code; archiving freezes a repo.
Rewriting branch protection can remove the rules that guard main.
A GitHub GraphQL mutation (deleteRepository, transferRepository, updateRepository and every other write), or a request Counterseal cannot read.
GitHub GraphQL over GET is not a normal client path.
Overwriting a CI secret silently changes what production deploys with.
Deletes a zone, DNS record, Worker, bucket, database or token.
Purging everything, a whole host or a URL prefix can take a site down under load.
Uploading over a Worker replaces production code.
Overwriting a DNS record can point a domain somewhere else.
Bucket lifecycle rules can delete objects; domain changes expose a bucket.
Rolling an API token breaks everything using it.
SQL against a production D1 database that is not a single plain read.
Importing an SQL file into a production D1 database runs SQL Counterseal cannot read.
Restoring a D1 database to an earlier point overwrites everything written since.
A Railway mutation other than a redeploy or restart, or a request Counterseal cannot read (PocketOS lost production to one volumeDelete).
A Railway mutation sent over GET.
Railway's API is GraphQL over POST; a PUT, PATCH or DELETE is not a normal client path.
Deletes customers, products, webhooks or cancels subscriptions.
Moves money.
Moves money.
Creating a payment intent with confirm=true charges the customer.
Refunds money.
Paying or voiding an invoice cannot be undone.
Issuing a credit note credits or refunds the customer.
Voiding a credit note cannot be undone.
Cancels a paying customer.
Schedules a paying customer to be cancelled.
Changing webhooks can silently stop order fulfilment.
Deletes a project, function, branch or secret.
SQL on the database that is not a single plain read (SELECT, WITH ... SELECT, EXPLAIN, SHOW).
A database migration runs schema changes (and any SQL) on production.
Pausing or restoring a project takes production offline.
Resetting the database password breaks every existing connection.
Changes production database, auth or network configuration.
Overwriting project secrets changes production configuration.
